subject: geography
title: Erosional & Depositional Landforms
welcome_lead: Identify cliffs, stacks, beaches and spits.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on coastal landforms, erosion and deposition.
final_note: Form follows process; rock structure matters.

concepts.def: Flat rocky shore exposed at low tide; result of cliff retreat.
Isolated pillar of resistant rock; e.g. Old Harry, Dorset.
Accumulation of sand or shingle in zone of wave action.
Beach extending across estuary/bay; recurved by changing wind direction.
Bar connecting island to mainland; Chesil Beach to Portland.
Rock layers perpendicular to coast; produces headlands and bays.

walkthroughs.body_html: Headland erosion: weakness exploited by hydraulic action -> cave -> arch -> stack -> stump. Old Harry Rocks (Dorset) shows full sequence in chalk. Wave-cut notch undercuts cliff; mass movement causes retreat leaving wave-cut platform up to 0.5 km wide.

Beach profile depends on sediment size and wave energy: shingle = steep, sand = gentle. Spurn Head (5.5 km) is recurved spit at Humber. Hurst Castle Spit (Hampshire) defends Solent. Tombolo at Chesil connects Portland; barrier beaches enclose Slapton Ley.

Discordant Dorset coast: chalk Ballard Down forms headland; clays of Swanage Bay erode rapidly. Concordant coast at Lulworth: harder Portland limestone outer barrier breached by sea forming Lulworth Cove. Rock structure (joints, dip, lithology) determines landform development.
